title: KV cache calibration: holistic FP8/INT8 latency vs quality trade-off experiments
creator: Asha Menon
description: End-to-end experiment ticket to validate KV-cache-only quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8 variants) with a focus on realistic calibration workflows, per-model profile selection, and systematic latency/quality trade-offs. This ticket covers dataset selection for calibration, automated calibration pipelines, eval harness for next-token and generation quality, and latency/throughput measurement across representative hardware stacks.
background: Previous experiments focused on microbench ablations (INT8 vs FP8) and asymmetric calibration. We need a complementary holistic validation that mimics real inference workloads: mixed prefix lengths, cache cold->warm transitions, variable batch sizes, and model variants. The goal is production-ready profile recommendations and runtime routing rules that pick quantized KV when acceptable.
goals: 1) Produce calibrated INT8 and FP8 KV profiles per-model that generalize across prefix distributions. 2) Quantify latency gains (p50/p95) and throughput changes vs baseline FP16/FP32. 3) Measure quality delta on next-token and end-to-end generation metrics and identify failure modes. 4) Produce a decision matrix for runtime kernel selection and fallback triggers.
hypothesis: FP8 KV profiles will offer a better quality/latency sweet spot for long contexts where dequantization kernel overhead is amortized, while INT8 will yield higher throughput on short prefixes but may introduce drift on long-cache lifecycles if scale calibration does not handle rare outliers.
calibration_dataset: Constructed calibration set of ~1500 examples combining: 1) 600 long-prefix continuations (8k context simulated) from CodeCorpus+Books, 2) 600 short-prefix/generation prompts (instruction style) from internal prompt-suite, 3) 300 chat-like turns to represent conversational cache reuse. Token distributions matched to production telemetry for top customers.
calibration_workflow_steps: Sample representative prefixes by context-length buckets (128, 512, 2048, 8192)
Run deterministic forward passes to capture key/value tensors per layer/head for each prefix sample
Apply per-layer and per-head scale estimators: max-abs, percentile-99.9, and MAD-based robust scaler
Evaluate symmetric vs asymmetric quantization maps and optional channel-wise scaling for heads with multi-modal activations
Emit candidate profiles (INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, FP8 e4m3 variants) and record quantization stats (saturation rate, dynamic range, outlier frequency)
Store profiles with metadata: model_version, context_bucket, calibration_set_id, estimator_type, and thermal stamps
measurement_plan: Quality: next-token cross-entropy on held-out next-token set, token-level accuracy on targeted synthetic tests, and subjective generation quality on 200 human-rated prompts
Robustness: drift over simulated long-generation (simulate 1024 incremental generate steps with cache reuse) and measure divergence against FP16 baseline
Latency: p50/p95 per-token latency, end-to-end request latency for streaming responses, kernel-level timings (dequant+matmul+re-quant), and GPU memory usage
Throughput: tokens/sec at batch sizes 1,4,16 across A100 and H100 pools
Failure modes: dropout cases where saturation >0.1% or where perplexity delta > 2% relative to FP16
acceptance_criteria: 1) Identify at most two profile variants per model+context-bucket with <=1% next-token perplexity regression and measurable latency improvement (>=8% p95 reduction) OR 2) Produce a justification report if quantized KV cannot meet target for any bucket. 3) Runtime decision matrix that maps model+context->profile with fallback rules and telemetry hooks.
approach: Implement an automated calibration pipeline in runtime-tests: a) exporter to collect KV tensors in-flight, b) offline calibration module to sweep estimators and generate profiles, c) eval harness that replays cached KV in quantized kernels to measure quality and latency. Use existing perf harness and add additional tracing to break down dequantization overhead. Run experiments across representative hardware and model families (Llama-2-13B, RW-7B variants).
experimental_results_summary: (work in progress) Initial runs on Llama-2-13B: FP8-e4m3 KV profile reduces median per-token latency by ~6-9% on H100 for long contexts (>=4096) and shows ~0.3% next-token perplexity regression. INT8 symmetric shows ~12% throughput improvement on short contexts but exhibits 1.5-2.3% perplexity regression on long simulated cache lifecycles when using max-abs calibration. Percentile-based calibration for INT8 recovers most of the quality gap at a modest increase in scale metadata and some runtime branching.
observations_and_tradeoffs: 1) Dequantization kernel cost is significant for tiny batch sizes; gains are realized when amortized over long KV matmuls. 2) FP8 requires careful e4m3 exponent bias handling — some kernels need refactoring to avoid underflow/overflow on head-normalized keys. 3) INT8 with channel-wise scaling reduces saturation but increases profile size and complicates runtime cache lookup. 4) Calibration set choice strongly affects long-context drift — outlier tokens (rare tokens, punctuation-heavy spans) dominate scale selection if not filtered.
next_steps: 1) Finalize percentile-based estimator (99.95) for INT8 long-context buckets and implement compact per-head metadata encoding. 2) Add an automated nightly job to validate profiles against streaming production-like traces. 3) Land kernel optimizations to reduce dequantization latency for batch-size=1 fast path. 4) Write runtime routing policy for: prefer FP8 for context>=2048 on H100; prefer INT8 for context<512 when percentile-calibrated.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: profiles tuned on synthetic calibration may fail on customer-specific token distributions. Mitigation: include sampled customer telemetry (anonymized) in calibration and add runtime fallback that detects quality drift and triggers on-the-fly re-calibration for that tenant.
